Let \(\vec a,\vec b,\vec c,\vec d\) be position vectors.  
\[
\vec{CA}=\vec a-\vec c=(\vec b-\vec c)-(\vec b-\vec a)
=(\vec e_1+3\vec e_2)-(2\vec e_1+k\vec e_2)
=-\vec e_1+(3-k)\vec e_2.
\]
Then
\[
\vec{AD}=\vec{CD}-\vec{CA}
=(2\vec e_1-\vec e_2)-\bigl(-\vec e_1+(3-k)\vec e_2\bigr)
=3\vec e_1+(k-4)\vec e_2.
\]
Since \(A,B,D\) are collinear, \(\vec{AB}=\lambda \vec{AD}\). Thus
\[
2\vec e_1+k\vec e_2=\lambda\bigl(3\vec e_1+(k-4)\vec e_2\bigr).
\]
Comparing coefficients gives \(2=3\lambda\), so \(\lambda=\frac23\), and
\[
k=\frac23(k-4)\implies 3k=2k-8\implies k=-8.
\]
\[
\boxed{-8}
\]
